input.quote: Except pursuant to or as expressly permitted by this Agreement, RevMed shall not, shall cause its Affiliates not to, conduct or agree to conduct, outside of the Collaboration, on its own or together with one or more Third Parties, the Research, Development or Commercialization of any product that contains a SHP2 Inhibitor, including any SHP1-SHP2 Dual Inhibitor that [***].
input.rationale: The only exclusivity covenant in the Agreement (Section 3.5(a)) binds RevMed, not us — it stops the counterparty from developing or commercializing SHP2 Inhibitor products outside the Collaboration, which benefits Sanofi and is not flagged. No covenant anywhere restricts Sanofi's freedom to research, develop, acquire or commercialize competing or other products: searches for "Sanofi shall not"-type restrictions, "Competing Product", "Non-SHP2 Same Class Product", "Other SHP2 Inhibitor" and field/territory limits return only vendor-side covenants, definitions and non-restrictive mechanics. This meets the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer). Two items noted but not deviations: (i) Section 12.2(d) lets RevMed terminate if Sanofi develops a Competing Product before commencing a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product — a termination trigger with an election to cure, not a prohibition on our business; and (ii) Section 15.2's change-of-control conditions require separation of the Acquired Party Family's SHP2 assets from Acquiror Family Competing Products, but these are mutual assignment/IP-perimeter conditions rather than a restraint on what businesses or products we may operate, buy or build.
